slides.title: Random variables and expectation
bullets: Lecture 03 · Probability Notebook
Numbers attached to outcomes, and their distributions
Averages: expected value and linearity
Spread: variance and standard deviation

slides.title: A random variable is a function
bullets: A random variable X assigns a number X(ω) to every outcome ω in Ω.
Nothing about X is random: the randomness is in which outcome occurs.
{X = k} is an event: the set of outcomes ω with X(ω) = k.
Two dice: X = first die, S = sum, M = maximum, D = first minus second.

slides.title: Probability mass function
bullets: The PMF of a discrete X is p(k) = P(X = k) for each value k.
Every p(k) ≥ 0, and the values of p add up to 1.
Sum of two dice: p(7) = 6/36 = 1/6, while p(2) = p(12) = 1/36.
Different random variables can have the same PMF.

slides.title: Expected value
bullets: E[X] = Σ k · P(X = k): the values of X weighted by their probabilities.
Equivalently, E[X] = Σ X(ω) · P({ω}) over all outcomes ω.
E[X] need not be a value that X can take.

slides.title: Expectation of a function of X
bullets: E[g(X)] = Σ g(k) · P(X = k): no new PMF is needed.
In general E[g(X)] ≠ g(E[X]): here (E[X])² = 49/4, not 91/6.

slides.title: Fair games
bullets: A bet is fair when the expected net gain is 0.
Pay 1 to roll a die; a six returns 6, so the net gain is 5 or −1.
E[gain] = 5 · 1/6 + (−1) · 5/6 = 0: the bet is fair.
A fair bet can still be risky: the mean says nothing about spread.

slides.title: Joint distributions
bullets: The joint PMF of X and Y is p(x, y) = P(X = x and Y = y).
Marginal PMF: P(X = x) = Σ_y p(x, y), summing out the other variable.
The marginals do not determine the joint PMF.

slides.title: Independent random variables
bullets: X and Y are independent when p(x, y) = P(X = x) · P(Y = y) for all x, y.
Two fair dice: every cell of the joint PMF is 1/36 = 1/6 · 1/6.
First die X and maximum M are dependent: P(X = 6, M = 1) = 0.

slides.title: Linearity of expectation
bullets: E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] for any random variables X and Y.
E[aX + b] = a · E[X] + b for constants a and b.
Independence is not needed.
Sum of two dice: E[S] = 7/2 + 7/2 = 7, with no PMF of S required.

slides.title: Indicator variables
bullets: The indicator of an event A is 1 if A occurs and 0 if it does not.
E[indicator of A] = 1 · P(A) + 0 · P(not A) = P(A).
Write a count as a sum of indicators; its mean is a sum of probabilities.
Fixed points of a random permutation of n items: n · 1/n = 1.

slides.title: Variance and standard deviation
bullets: Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²], where μ = E[X].
Shortcut: Var(X) = E[X²] − (E[X])².
SD(X) = √Var(X), in the same units as X.
One fair die: Var(X) = 91/6 − 49/4 = 35/12, so SD ≈ 1.71.

slides.title: Variance of sums
bullets: Var(aX + b) = a² · Var(X): shifting does not change the spread.
If X and Y are independent, Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
Without independence it can fail: Var(X + X) = 4 · Var(X).

slides.title: Summary
bullets: A random variable is a number attached to each outcome.
PMFs and joint PMFs describe it; marginals sum out the other variable.
Expectation is always linear.
Variances add for independent random variables.
